items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: And, of course, the trio that I had there: Walter Booker on bass and Jimmy Cobbs (sic) on drums and John Hicks on piano, they had the right attitude.

ctx.x: All right, now, these last few months you've come up a number of times and played at the Tin Palace, at the West End, and now at the Vanguard. I wonder, in terms of being in New York these past few months, what changes you notice from the time that you were here before.

Well, what I noticed this time was that, you know, the wheel always turns, the wheel never stops turning, but people want to go back to basic things and they want to go back to soul and people, I mean they want a little more romantic music, mainly, that's what they want. They want something that they can actually feel, outside of electronics and all of these things. But they want something that they can feel and the stimulus for that, I can feel it, you know. And when I came to the Tin Palace the first time in…

New Year's Eve," you know, they'd never seen so many musicians in the Tin Palace. But most of these people they were, you know, my peers or they came up under me and it was like a festive thing and it was very heart warming. Then when I went up to the West End which is an establishment that's been there for many years, everybody was very warm and I saw some old friends. I saw Beverly Peer, who's with Bobby Short...
